checks: Original 655fcaee47bd2237 §2 has the same base-fixing affine form, stationary mixture, anchor hypothesis and averaged centroid consequence.

Positive mixture weights force each pushforward support inside the finite union of measured fibers. Continuity and full support put the image of every point of an original fiber in the pushforward support, so base preservation gives the required inclusions.

At the marked base the stationarity identity restricts to uniform volume, and each affine map fixes the interior mark. The same-wave predecessor then gives modulus-one determinant for the common linear part of each map.

At every other fiber the determinant applies to its full-dimensional body. A proper closed convex inclusion would miss a neighborhood meeting the interior, with positive volume. Hence every fiber is preserved bijectively.
Preservation of uniform volume fixes each ordinary centroid. Averaging the centroid identities and imposing zero averaged A gives the stated affine graph.

dependencies.hypotheses: Same-wave interior-fixed stationary affine rigidity. At p all component maps preserve the anchor by inclusion, have the same interior fixed point, and their positive-weight pushforwards reproduce its uniform volume. The exact frozen predecessor proof was independently reviewed; admission of this dependent claim requires that predecessor's approval.

overlap.comparison: Provides the form of mixed-lattice automorphisms. It does not show that a stationary affine mixture consists of such automorphisms on the actual fibers.

review_method: Independent exact-byte proof review, source and predecessor comparison, and exact arithmetic replay where applicable.
summary: One interior-fixed stationary fiber forces all fiber inclusions to be volume-preserving equalities.
